docs.text: Driver FDO2 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the PyroScience FDO2-G2 and the legacy FDO2 optical oxygen modules on UART. It starts the module, reads oxygen and temperature, checks the status word and guards the commands that write flash, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes on the UART; it does the rest: the power-up wait, the command lines, the checksum, the status policy, retries and timeouts. docs.text: API guide ¶ The driver's calls by task: start, measure, read the identity and handle errors. Datasheet sections this page relies on From PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5: Volume fraction from partial pressure: 2 Specifications, note on % O2 before Environment, p. 6 VERS: device, channels, firmware, sensors: 4.3 Commands, #VERS, p. 11 ¶ IDNR: the unique id: 4.3 Commands, #IDNR, p. 11 ¶ MOXY: oxygen, temperature, status: 4.3 Commands, #MOXY, p. 11 ¶ MRAW: phase, signals, pressure, humidity: 4.3 Commands, #MRAW, p. 12 ¶ LOGO: the status LED: 4.3 Commands, #LOGO, p. 13 ¶ RDUM and #WRUM: 64 user words: 4.3 Commands, #RDUM, #WRUM, p. 14 ¶ All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Start ¶ FDO2<YourPort> sensor(port) stores the port and the Config and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the only start-up call: it powers the module if your port has the supply hook, waits for the power-up, reads #VERS and #IDNR , checks the device and learns what the firmware offers. Every other I/O call returns NotInitialized before it has succeeded. Deinitialize() goes back. Resync() recovers a line in an unknown state and PowerCycle() restarts the module. Measure oxygen ¶ MeasureOxygen() returns an Oxygen : o2_mhpa (oxygen partial pressure in 0.001 hPa), temperature_mc (0.001 degC), the Status , its Quality and warming_up . The call fails with SensorFault when the status word is not acceptable under the status policy , and with OutOfRange when oxygen or temperature is outside the windows in Config . quickstart.cpp #include "fdo2.hpp" // Returns 0 and the oxygen partial pressure in 0.001 hPa and the temperature in 0.001 degC. int read_oxygen ( MyPort & port , int32_t & o2_mhpa , int32_t & temperature_mc ) { fdo2 :: FDO2 < MyPort > sensor ( port ); // no I/O yet // 1. Waits for the module's power-up, reads #VERS and #IDNR and checks the device. if ( auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Timeout or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring and the 3 V levels } // 2. One #MOXY: oxygen, temperature and the status word. const auto o = sensor . MeasureOxygen (); if ( ! o ) { return static_cast < int > ( o . error ); // SensorFault: see the status word; OutOfRange; Timeout } o2_mhpa = o . value . o2_mhpa ; // 10^-3 hPa temperature_mc = o . value . temperature_mc ; // 10^-3 degC return 0 ; } Oxygen as a fraction ¶ api_guide.cpp // The oxygen fraction in 0.001 percent, from the module's own pressure reading. fdo2 :: Result < int32_t > OxygenFraction ( Sensor & sensor ) { return sensor . MeasureVolumePercentMilli (); // needs a good status and a plausible pressure } MeasureVolumePercentMilli() returns the oxygen fraction in 0.001 percent: the partial pressure divided by the total pressure, from #MRAW . It needs a good status and a pressure inside Config::pressure_min_ubar .. pressure_max_ubar . Set pressure_reference_ubar to use your own pressure instead of the module's. It is a dry-gas fraction. Venting capillary The module's pressure sensor measures through the venting capillary at the back of the housing. The fraction is right only when the pressure at the capillary equals the pressure at the sensing membrane (datasheet section 2). In a sealed or pressurised vessel with the capillary outside, they differ: set pressure_reference_ubar to the pressure at the membrane, or use the oxygen partial pressure itself. Raw values ¶ api_guide.cpp // A full reading: oxygen, temperature, phase shift, signals, pressure and humidity. bool ReadAll ( Sensor & sensor , fdo2 :: Raw & out ) { const auto raw = sensor . MeasureRaw (); if ( ! raw ) { return false ; // raw.error says why } out = raw . value ; return out . oxygen . quality == fdo2 :: Quality :: Good ; } MeasureRaw() adds the phase shift ( dphi_mdeg ), the signal and ambient light (microvolts), the pressure (microbar) and the humidity (0.001 %RH). The pressure is not a gate of this call; it is checked when you ask for a fraction or a calibration. Identity ¶ api_guide.cpp // The module's identity is read once at start-up and kept. bool IsG2 ( Sensor & sensor ) { const fdo2 :: Identity & id = sensor . GetIdentity (); return id . caps . set_mode && ( id . version . firmware >= 355 ); } GetIdentity() returns what start-up read: Version (device id, channels, firmware, sensors), the unique id and Capabilities . ReadVersion() , ReadUniqueId() and Identify() ask the module again. Handle errors ¶ api_guide.cpp const char * Explain ( fdo2 :: Error error ) { switch ( error ) { case fdo2 :: Error :: Timeout : return "no reply: wiring, 3 V levels, power" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: Crc : return "a corrupted reply: noise on the line" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: SensorFault : return "the status word says the reading is not valid" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: NotPermitted : return "a flash write needs Config::allow_persistent_writes" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: StateUnknown : return "call Resync()" ; default : break ; } return fdo2 :: ToString ( error ); } Every call returns a Result<T> ( value and error ); check ok() before you use the value. The full list is on Status and errors . Reads are repeated up to Config::retries times when the failure may be transient; writes to flash never are. Next ¶ Calibration , Settings , Non-blocking use . docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one call through them and the choices behind them. The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/fdo2.hpp public calls ; inc/fdo2_uart_interface.hpp UartInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Core inc/fdo2.hpp , src/fdo2.ipp Lifecycle, the state machine, measurements, calibration, settings, retries, errors Protocol inc/fdo2_protocol.hpp CRC-16, command encoding, the line assembler and the reply parser Types inc/fdo2_types.hpp , inc/fdo2_detail.hpp Error , Result<T> , Config , Status , conversions, compile-time helpers Port contract inc/fdo2_uart_interface.hpp The CRTP base, CtrlPin , GpioSignal , the UartPort concept Platform port Your class The UART, and optionally the clock, delay, baud rate, supply switch and log Kconfig layer inc/fdo2_kconfig.hpp Optional: a Config from ESP-IDF menuconfig The protocol layer has no state and no port: the tests drive it alone. One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as FDO2<Port> participant Port as Your port App->>Core: MeasureOxygen() Core->>Port: FlushInput() Core->>Port: Write("#MOXY") loop until CR or deadline Core->>Port: Read(buffer, max, timeout) Port-->>Core: n bytes end Note over Core: assemble the line, check CRC, parse Note over Core: status policy, plausibility windows Core-->>App: Result<Oxygen> Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by a concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. One state machine, two ways to drive it. The blocking calls are the start call plus a loop over Poll() with the port's delay, so both paths run the same code ( Non-blocking use ). A parser that only reads. It returns a value or a reason; the core decides what to do about it. Flash writes are guarded. Opt-in, a budget, never repeated ( Calibration ). One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws. No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state. docs.text: Calibration ¶ How to calibrate the module in air or with two points, and why every calibration call needs your consent first. Datasheet sections this page relies on From PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5: CALO: zero calibration: 4.3 Commands, #CALO, p. 14 ¶ CAHI: high calibration: 4.3 Commands, #CAHI, p. 15 ¶ Flash endurance and interrupted writes: 4.3 Commands, WARNING, p. 16 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Consent and the write budget ¶ #CALO and #CAHI write the module's flash, and so do #CRCE , #WRUM , #BCST and #SETM . The flash survives only a limited number of writes (the module's own limit, about 20000 cycles in all). So the driver sends these commands only when you ask for it in the Config : configuration.cpp fdo2 :: Config WritableConfig () { fdo2 :: Config c {}; c . allow_persistent_writes = true ; // every flash-writing call needs this c . max_flash_writes = 4 ; // and is counted against this budget (about 20000 cycles in all) return c ; } allow_persistent_writes is false by default. A flash-writing call returns NotPermitted and sends nothing. max_flash_writes (1 to 64, default 8) is the number of such calls the driver sends in its lifetime. FlashWritesUsed() shows the count. A write counts when it is sent, even if the port fails, because the module may have received it. A flash write is never repeated. If the reply is lost, the call returns the original error (for example Timeout ) and the state becomes StateUnknown ; call Resync() and read the module back before you try again. Vendor warnings ¶ The datasheet (section 4.3, Commands, and the warning that follows it) says, and the driver follows: Flash endurance is about 20,000 flash cycles in all, triggered by #CALO , #CAHI , #CRCE , #SETM and #BCST (and by #WRUM , which the datasheet describes as one cycle per call). Use them only when needed. max_flash_writes is a guard against a loop in your code, not the vendor figure: its limit of 64 per driver lifetime is far below 20,000. A power loss during a flash cycle can corrupt the flash. Keep the supply stable while one runs. The driver refuses Deinitialize() with Busy while a write is pending, and PowerCycle() waits for it to end ( Settings ). Always evaluate the reply. A write without its echo may have corrupted the flash: the driver reports the original error and the state StateUnknown . #CALO and #CAHI replace the factory calibration. The datasheet asks for at least 5 minutes of steady measuring in the reference medium before the command, and the command takes up to 10 seconds. The guard before every flash write ¶ A wrong calibration is stored in the module for good, so the driver checks before it sends #CALO or #CAHI : It reads #VERS and compares it with the identity found at start-up. A different module on the line, or a module that has reset without the driver seeing it (a power glitch, for example), ends in StateUnknown or DeviceIdMismatch and nothing is written. It reads #MOXY . The status must be acceptable, and the sensor must have been powered for the warm-up time of 3 minutes (datasheet section 2): earlier the call returns NotReady . The measured oxygen partial pressure must lie within Config::cal_window_pct percent (default 20, at least cal_window_min_mhpa , default 5000 milli-hPa) of the value you are about to store. A sensor still in air cannot be calibrated as nitrogen, and the reverse: the call returns OutOfRange and nothing is written. Only then does it send the write, and it counts it. The guard reads #MOXY but not #VERS before a calibration, and its warm-up test counts the time since the driver powered the module, using the host's clock (the datasheet gives no uptime value to read). A module that was swapped or reset after start-up is therefore seen only through the plausibility window and the status word. The other flash commands ( #CRCE , #WRUM , #BCST , #SETM ) get the identity check (1). The one exception is #BCST 0 while the module streams, which is sent as it is because no reply can be read in a stream. CalibrateHigh() accepts 10 to 2000 hPa (10000 to 2000000 in 0.001 hPa): a standard outside the range of a real calibration gas returns InvalidArgument . Before you calibrate ¶ Keep the sensor in the reference medium until the readings are steady. The datasheet asks for five minutes. steady_s is the time you have waited; a value below Config::min_steady_s (default 300) returns InvalidArgument and sends nothing. The status must be good. CalibrateAir() returns SensorFault otherwise. The sensor must be warmed up (3 minutes after power-up), or the call returns NotReady . Calibration changes the module's stored calibration. Not verified on hardware: nobody has run these calls against a module yet. One point in air ¶ calibration.cpp // One high point in ambient air; the sensor has been in it for at least five minutes. fdo2 :: Error CalibrateInAir ( Sensor & sensor ) { // Reads the module's pressure, takes 20.95 % oxygen (dry air) and sends #CAHI. return sensor . CalibrateAir ( 300 ). error ; // NotPermitted unless allowed in the Config } CalibrateAir() reads #MRAW for the pressure, computes the oxygen partial pressure of dry air at that pressure (20.95 percent by default, kDryAirO2Ppm ) and sends #CAHI . docs.text: #CALO and #CAHI write the module's flash, and so do #CRCE , #WRUM , #BCST and #SETM . The flash survives only a limited number of writes (the module's own limit, about 20000 cycles in all). So the driver sends these commands only when you ask for it in the Config : configuration.cpp fdo2 :: Config WritableConfig () { fdo2 :: Config c {}; c . allow_persistent_writes = true ; // every flash-writing call needs this c . max_flash_writes = 4 ; // and is counted against this budget (about 20000 cycles in all) return c ; } allow_persistent_writes is false by default. A flash-writing call returns NotPermitted and sends nothing. max_flash_writes (1 to 64, default 8) is the number of such calls the driver sends in its lifetime. FlashWritesUsed() shows the count. A write counts when it is sent, even if the port fails, because the module may have received it. A flash write is never repeated. If the reply is lost, the call returns the original error (for example Timeout ) and the state becomes StateUnknown ; call Resync() and read the module back before you try again.
docs.title: Consent and the write budget

docs.text: The datasheet (section 4.3, Commands, and the warning that follows it) says, and the driver follows: Flash endurance is about 20,000 flash cycles in all, triggered by #CALO , #CAHI , #CRCE , #SETM and #BCST (and by #WRUM , which the datasheet describes as one cycle per call). Use them only when needed. max_flash_writes is a guard against a loop in your code, not the vendor figure: its limit of 64 per driver lifetime is far below 20,000. A power loss during a flash cycle can corrupt the flash. Keep the supply stable while one runs. The driver refuses Deinitialize() with Busy while a write is pending, and PowerCycle() waits for it to end ( Settings ). Always evaluate the reply. A write without its echo may have corrupted the flash: the driver reports the original error and the state StateUnknown . #CALO and #CAHI replace the factory calibration. The datasheet asks for at least 5 minutes of steady measuring in the reference medium before the command, and the command takes up to 10 seconds.

docs.text: A wrong calibration is stored in the module for good, so the driver checks before it sends #CALO or #CAHI : It reads #VERS and compares it with the identity found at start-up. A different module on the line, or a module that has reset without the driver seeing it (a power glitch, for example), ends in StateUnknown or DeviceIdMismatch and nothing is written. It reads #MOXY . The status must be acceptable, and the sensor must have been powered for the warm-up time of 3 minutes (datasheet section 2): earlier the call returns NotReady . The measured oxygen partial pressure must lie within Config::cal_window_pct percent (default 20, at least cal_window_min_mhpa , default 5000 milli-hPa) of the value you are about to store. A sensor still in air cannot be calibrated as nitrogen, and the reverse: the call returns OutOfRange and nothing is written. Only then does it send the write, and it counts it. The guard reads #MOXY but not #VERS before a calibration, and its warm-up test counts the time since the driver powered the module, using the host's clock (the datasheet gives no uptime value to read). A module that was swapped or reset after start-up is therefore seen only through the plausibility window and the status word. The other flash commands ( #CRCE , #WRUM , #BCST , #SETM ) get the identity check (1). The one exception is #BCST 0 while the module streams, which is sent as it is because no reply can be read in a stream. CalibrateHigh() accepts 10 to 2000 hPa (10000 to 2000000 in 0.001 hPa): a standard outside the range of a real calibration gas returns InvalidArgument .
docs.title: The guard before every flash write

docs.text: Keep the sensor in the reference medium until the readings are steady. The datasheet asks for five minutes. steady_s is the time you have waited; a value below Config::min_steady_s (default 300) returns InvalidArgument and sends nothing. The status must be good. CalibrateAir() returns SensorFault otherwise. The sensor must be warmed up (3 minutes after power-up), or the call returns NotReady . Calibration changes the module's stored calibration. Not verified on hardware: nobody has run these calls against a module yet.

[Unreleased] ¶ Added ¶ First version: a C++20 driver for the PyroScience FDO2-G2 and the legacy FDO2 optical oxygen modules on UART. docs.text: Contract ¶ What the FDO2 driver promises, what it needs and the rules a caller follows. Datasheet sections this page relies on From PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5: Flash endurance and interrupted writes: 4.3 Commands, WARNING, p. 16 ERRO codes: 4.4 Error Codes, Table 1, p. 17 ¶ All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. It checks the configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the UART up, waits for the power-up, reads #VERS and #IDNR and checks the device. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the module returns NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() has succeeded. A command that writes flash is sent only with Config::allow_persistent_writes and inside Config::max_flash_writes ; it is never repeated. A write that ends without an echo leaves the state StateUnknown until Resync() or a power cycle. Before every flash write the driver re-reads #VERS and checks the identity; before #CALO and #CAHI it also reads #MOXY and refuses a warming-up or implausible reading ( Calibration ). Deinitialize() returns Busy while a flash write is pending, and a failed EnsureInitialized() or an aborted one leaves the driver uninitialised, so the next call identifies the module again. Reads are repeated only for transient failures, at most Config::retries times. Every port failure propagates as Bus ; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read. Every wait is bounded by the allowance of its command plus the line time plus Config::margin_ms . Config{} follows the datasheets; StatusPolicy::Datasheet is the default. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error for the blocking calls; a missing NowUs() selects Poll(elapsed_us) ; a missing SetBaudRate() gives Unsupported ; a missing Log() logs nothing. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates fdo2_version.h Your port The UART within the bus requirements, a delay, and optionally a clock, the baud rate, the supply switch and logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the organisation. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex. Nothing may run in an interrupt handler: the blocking calls wait. Separate objects share no state; each needs its own UART, because the protocol has no addressing. Errors ¶ fdo2::Error inside fdo2::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; the chip-specific values start at 16. The full list, with what to do about each, is on Status and errors . Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, the Config , the identity, a line buffer of 800 characters and a 64-byte receive window: about one kilobyte, mostly the line buffer. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Not verified on hardware ¶ See Limitations . Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

Datasheet sections this page relies on Measuring range, accuracy and warm-up: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 2 Specifications, Analytical Performance, p. 5 Supply voltage and current: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 2 Specifications, Interface, p. 6 Temperature and pressure limits, humidity: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 2 Specifications, Environment, p. 6 Mechanics, connector part and weight: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 2 Specifications, Mechanical, p. 7 Cross-sensitivity and chemical compatibility: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 3 Cross-Sensitivity and Chemical Compatibility, p. 8 Power-up time: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4 Communication Interface, p. 10 Connector, pins and signal levels: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 7 Mechanical Dimensions and Electrical Interface, drawing and pin table, p. 20 Mechanical drawing: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 7 Mechanical Dimensions and Electrical Interface, drawings, p. 20 Supply below 3.3 V and readings: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 2 Specifications, Interface, WARNING, p. 6 UART levels: 3.0 V, 3.3 V maximum on RXD: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.2 Voltage Tolerance of UART RX Pin (ERRATA), p. 19 Replacement of the FDO2 by the FDO2-G2: PyroScience PCN-FDO2-002 n/a, Product change notification, text, p. 1 Flow-through cell accessory: PyroScience Data Sheet_FDO2_FTC n/a, Flow-through cell data sheet, whole document, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . RXD tolerates 3.3 V at most The module's UART runs at 3.0 V. The RXD pin (pin 3) must not see more than 3.3 V. A controller with 5 V outputs needs a divider or a level shifter in front of RXD ( the 5 V circuit ). The legacy FDO2's datasheet (section 6.2, all modules) corrects an earlier "5 V tolerant" statement, found in versions up to 17 (April 2023), to "max. 3.3 V". The driver cannot check the wiring; the port examples assert kMaxLogicLevelMv so the number is in your code. Pins ¶ The module has a four-pin connector. The mating plug is the vendor's to name (see section 7 of the datasheet); this page does not give a part number. Not verified on hardware: the wiring below follows the datasheet. FDO2 pinout, Module, 4-pin Figure description and sources The FDO2 seen from the top, in its Module, 4-pin package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/fdo2_uart_interface.hpp . Module, 4-pin, 4 pins (7 Mechanical Dimensions and Electrical Interface, drawing and pin table, p. 20 ). Pin Name Type (domain) Function Driver hook If unused Datasheet 1 GND ground Ground - - 7, p. 20 2 TXD digital out (UART 3.0 V) Module transmit: 3.0 V UART data to the host (host RX) Read() Leave open 7, p. 20 3 RXD digital in (UART 3.0 V) Module receive: UART data from the host, 3.0 V levels, absolute maximum 3.3 V (host TX) Write() - 7, p. 20 4 VCC power (VCC) Supply 3.3 V to 5.0 V; below 3.3 V the oxygen readings can be wrong. Optionally switched by the port's power hook GpioSet(CtrlPin::Power) - 7, p. 20 Source of this table and of the chip figures: docs/hardware.yml . Supply ¶ VCC takes 3.3 V to 5.0 V. Below 3.3 V the oxygen readings can be wrong, and the module has no supply reading, so the driver cannot detect it. After power-up the module needs about one second before it answers; the driver waits Config::power_up_ms (1500 ms by default). Readings in the first three minutes have reduced accuracy: Oxygen::warming_up is true for that time. A load switch on the supply is optional. If your port has GpioSet(CtrlPin::Power, ...) , PowerCycle() switches the supply off for Config::power_off_ms and on again, and EnsureInitialized() waits the power-up time. Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Baud rate 19200 after every power-up; SetBaudRate() can raise it until the next power-up Frame 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no handshake Levels 3.0 V; 3.3 V absolute maximum on RXD Messages ASCII, ended by one carriage return Receive buffer At least 800 bytes ( kRxBufferBytes ): the longest reply The commands are on the Protocol page. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( fdo2_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-fdo2.git external/driver-fdo2 git submodule update --init external/driver-fdo2 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-fdo2 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE fdo2::fdo2 ) fdo2::fdo2 is an alias of the fdo2 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect FDO2_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver FDO2_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-fdo2 -B build-fdo2 cmake --install build-fdo2 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( fdo2 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE fdo2::fdo2 ) The target is fdo2::fdo2 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated fdo2_version.h go to include/fdo2/inc/ , the template implementation to include/fdo2/src/fdo2.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-fdo2) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-fdo2 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-fdo2.git components/fdo2 fdo2 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml fdo2 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : fdo2 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-fdo2.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES fdo2 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/fdo2_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into fdo2_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = fdo2 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Limitations ¶ What the driver does not do, what it cannot verify and where the documentation has a known gap. Datasheet sections this page relies on Cross-sensitivity and chemical compatibility: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 3 Cross-Sensitivity and Chemical Compatibility, p. 8 Flash endurance and interrupted writes: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, WARNING, p. 16 Firmware revision history of the G2: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 5 Released Firmware Revisions Changes, p. 18 Errata: noise at two temperatures: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 6 ERRATA, 6.1 Increased Noise at Specific Temperatures, p. 19 Warnings: no medical or safety use: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 8 Warnings, p. 21 Supply below 3.3 V and readings: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 2 Specifications, Interface, WARNING, p. 6 Firmware revision history: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 5 Released Firmware Revisions Changes, p. 17 Errata: broadcast send and receive conflict (firmware 3.51): PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.1 Firmware Bug Broadcast Send and Receive Conflict (FW 3.51), p. 19 Errata: error handling of the internal temperature sensor: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.3 Error Handling of Internal Temperature Sensor, p. 20 Low-pass filter change and the noise erratum: PyroScience PCN-FDO2-G2-001 n/a, Product change notification, text, p. 1 Replacement of the FDO2 by the FDO2-G2: PyroScience PCN-FDO2-002 n/a, Product change notification, text, p. 1 Modbus extension module (a different interface): PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-EXT v5, 1 INTRODUCTION, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . What the driver does not do ¶ No compensation inputs. The module's firmware has no command to set salinity, pressure or temperature for a reading. The driver reports what the module reports. MeasureVolumePercentMilli() computes a fraction from the module's own pressure; it is a dry-gas fraction and does not model humidity. It is right only when the venting capillary at the back of the housing sees the same pressure as the membrane; otherwise set pressure_reference_ubar . No supply check. Below 3.3 V the readings can be wrong (datasheet section 2). The module has no supply reading, so the driver cannot warn you. No wiring check. Over-voltage on RXD is not detectable from software. Late replies. A reply that arrives after the deadline is drained before the next request, but a module that answers later than the allowance plus the margin is reported as Timeout . Raise Config::command_ms or the matching allowance if your module is slower. One module per line. The protocol has no addressing. Use one UART per module. No unit conversion beyond what the module gives. Values are integers: 0.001 hPa, 0.001 degC, microvolts, microbar. inc/fdo2_float.hpp does not exist; convert in your own code. Not verified on hardware ¶ No module has been connected to this driver. The behaviour comes from the datasheets and from a model of the module that the tests use. The model is written from the datasheets and not from the driver, but both can share a misreading. Every behaviour the datasheets leave open is a setting in Config or a documented choice; the Calibration , Settings and Status pages say which. The bench steps that confirm them are listed in the build report. The module figures ¶ The module is round with a four-pin connector, and the chip-diagram renderer draws packages with pins on the sides of a rectangle. So the pinout figure puts the four contacts in one row, as the datasheet draws them, and the outline figure draws a square of the module's diameter. A module view with a round body is a follow-up for the shared tooling. Firmware differences ¶ The driver covers firmware 3.28 to 3.57. GetIdentity().caps says what the connected firmware offers: user memory, broadcast, a stored checksum setting, calibration errors, #SETM and a reliable temperature flag. Firmware affected by the low-temperature noise erratum (8 to 15 degC) is flagged in Identity::noise_erratum ; the driver does not change readings for it.

docs.text: No compensation inputs. The module's firmware has no command to set salinity, pressure or temperature for a reading. The driver reports what the module reports. MeasureVolumePercentMilli() computes a fraction from the module's own pressure; it is a dry-gas fraction and does not model humidity. It is right only when the venting capillary at the back of the housing sees the same pressure as the membrane; otherwise set pressure_reference_ubar . No supply check. Below 3.3 V the readings can be wrong (datasheet section 2). The module has no supply reading, so the driver cannot warn you. No wiring check. Over-voltage on RXD is not detectable from software. Late replies. A reply that arrives after the deadline is drained before the next request, but a module that answers later than the allowance plus the margin is reported as Timeout . Raise Config::command_ms or the matching allowance if your module is slower. One module per line. The protocol has no addressing. Use one UART per module. No unit conversion beyond what the module gives. Values are integers: 0.001 hPa, 0.001 degC, microvolts, microbar. inc/fdo2_float.hpp does not exist; convert in your own code.

docs.text: Non-blocking use ¶ How to run the driver from a super-loop or a task without waiting inside a call. Datasheet sections this page relies on From PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5: Power-up time: 4 Communication Interface, p. 10 BCST: broadcast mode: 4.3 Commands, #BCST, p. 15 ¶ Measurement duration: 4.3 Commands, #SETM, modes, p. 16 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Two ways to call ¶ Every operation has a blocking form and a start form: Blocking Start Result EnsureInitialized() BeginInitialize() Identity MeasureOxygen() StartMeasureOxygen() GetOxygen() MeasureRaw() StartMeasureRaw() GetRaw() CalibrateZero() , CalibrateHigh() StartCalibrateZero() , StartCalibrateHigh() none SetCrcEnabled() , SetBroadcast() , SetBaudRate() , SetMeasurementMode() Start...() none ReadUserMemory() , WriteUserMemory() StartReadUserMemory() , StartWriteUserMemory() GetUserMemory() The blocking forms need the port's DelayUs hook: calling one from a port without it is a compile error. They wait for the module's reply, which takes up to 300 ms for a measurement and up to 10 s for a calibration. Poll ¶ A start call sends the request and returns. Poll() then reads what has arrived and moves the state forward. It returns Ok(false) while the operation is pending, Ok(true) when it ended, and an error when it failed. With a clock in the port ( NowUs ), call Poll() with no argument; it measures its own time. Without one, call Poll(elapsed_us) with the time since the last call. non_blocking.cpp // Start-up and one measurement per second, without blocking the loop. class OxygenTask { public : explicit OxygenTask ( TickPort & port ) : sensor_ ( port ) {} // Call from the super-loop every few milliseconds. void Step () { const uint32_t elapsed_us = platform_ticks_us (); if ( state_ == Phase :: Start ) { if ( sensor_ . BeginInitialize ()) { state_ = Phase :: Starting ; } return ; } const auto p = sensor_ . Poll ( elapsed_us ); if ( ! p ) { state_ = Phase :: Start ; // the operation failed: p.error; start again return ; } if ( ! p . value ) { return ; // still waiting for the module } if ( state_ == Phase :: Starting ) { state_ = Phase :: Idle ; } else if ( state_ == Phase :: Measuring ) { last_o2_mhpa_ = sensor_ . GetOxygen (). value . o2_mhpa ; state_ = Phase :: Idle ; } else if ( sensor_ . StartMeasureOxygen ()) { state_ = Phase :: Measuring ; } else { // the start was refused (busy): try again at the next poll } } [[ nodiscard ]] int32_t last_o2_mhpa () const { return last_o2_mhpa_ ; } private : enum class Phase : uint8_t { Start , Starting , Idle , Measuring }; fdo2 :: FDO2 < TickPort > sensor_ ; Phase state_ = Phase :: Start ; int32_t last_o2_mhpa_ = 0 ; }; non_blocking.cpp // With a clock in the port (NowUs), Poll() takes no argument. bool Tick ( fdo2 :: FDO2 < MyPort >& sensor ) { if ( sensor . IsInitialized () && ( sensor . Pending () == fdo2 :: OperationKind :: None )) { return sensor . StartMeasureRaw (). ok (); } return false ; } Only one operation runs at a time. A start call while one is pending returns Busy . Pending() names it and AbortOperation() drops it. States ¶ GetState() returns one of seven states. The driver's states Figure description and sources Each box is a State of fdo2::FDO2, read from the enumeration in inc/fdo2_types.hpp; each arrow is a call or an event that moves it. Start-up goes through PoweringUp to Idle. An operation (Start* or a blocking call) puts the driver in Waiting; a good reply returns it to Idle. A timeout, a CRC error or a refused line sends it through Draining, where input is discarded until the line is quiet, so a late reply is never read as the next answer. A flash-writing command or a baud change that ended without a confirmed echo leaves StateUnknown, which only Resync() or a power cycle ends. While the module streams, Idle is reported as Streaming. The transitions are fixed in this figure and checked against the names used in src/fdo2.ipp. Drawn from: inc/fdo2_types.hpp State ; src/fdo2.ipp State transitions ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/state-machine.py . State Meaning Uninitialized Nothing started, or Deinitialize() ran PoweringUp Waiting for the module's power-up ( Config::power_up_ms ) Idle Ready for a call Waiting A request is out; waiting for its reply (a flash write first runs a guard read) Streaming The module sends #MRAW lines by itself Draining Waiting for bytes of a late reply to stop before the next request StateUnknown A flash write or baud change ended with no echo; Resync() Deinitialize() returns Busy while a flash write may still be running, that is until its echo has arrived or its allowance has run down. On a port without NowUs() the time moves only through Poll(elapsed_us) , so a caller that does not poll stays Busy ; FlashWritePending() shows whether the wait is over. Timing of one request ¶ One command and its reply Figure description and sources A transaction is five steps, left to right. The driver drops what is in the receive buffer, writes the command and its carriage return, then waits for the module: the module echoes the command, with its values, and ends the reply with one carriage return. The wait is the characters' airtime at the current baud rate, plus the module's processing allowance for the command (command_ms, measurement_ms, calibration_ms, flash_ms or logo_ms of the Config), plus margin_ms. The numbers shown are the Config defaults, read from inc/fdo2_types.hpp. A reply that does not end in time is a Timeout: the driver drains the line, and sends an idempotent read again when retries allow. Drawn from: inc/fdo2_types.hpp Config ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/transaction-timing.py . The deadline of a request is the allowance for its command ( measurement_ms , calibration_ms , flash_ms , ...) plus the time the line needs for the bytes plus Config::margin_ms . docs.text: Platforms ¶ The driver is MCU-agnostic: inc/ and src/ contain no SDK, RTOS or vendor header. A platform is three optional pieces around it, and only examples/<platform>/ holds platform code. Piece Where What it is Port examples/<platform>/ The class that implements the bus hooks for that MCU or OS ( Porting ) Example examples/<platform>/ A program that runs the driver there, built by CI Build integration the root CMakeLists.txt How that platform's build system finds the driver What exists today ¶ Platform Port Example Build integration Built by CI Host (Linux, macOS, Windows) examples/host/host_fdo2_port.hpp (simulated chip) examples/host/ Plain CMake yes, run as a test ESP32 (ESP-IDF) examples/esp32/main/esp32_fdo2_port.hpp examples/esp32/ Root CMakeLists.txt under ESP_PLATFORM (component) yes STM32, RP2040, nRF, other MCUs write one ( Porting ) none yet Plain CMake no Plain CMake ( add_subdirectory() or find_package() , see Installation ) covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and host builds. The root CMakeLists.txt also covers ESP-IDF: under ESP_PLATFORM it registers the repository as a component (a repository scaffolded without the ESP32 platform adds that branch back from the template when it needs it). Zephyr modules, Arduino library manifests and PlatformIO manifests are added only when a product needs them, and an example is added only together with a CI job that builds it. Add a platform ¶ The add-port skill has the details per MCU. In short: Create examples/<platform>/ with the port ( <platform>_fdo2_port.hpp ), a small example program and a README with the wiring and the expected output. The folder is self-contained: it carries its own port and builds on its own. Build it in CI: a job in .github/workflows/ that builds the example, needed by the CI gate . A platform that CI does not build is not added. If its build system cannot use the root CMakeLists.txt , add the smallest manifest it needs, and say why in the pull request. Never put platform code in inc/ or src/ . Add a row to the table above and a page section if the platform needs one.

docs.text: Porting ¶ How to write the port class that connects the driver to your MCU's UART, clock and pins. Datasheet sections this page relies on UART framing, echo and terminator: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.1 General Definitions, p. 10 BAUD: the eleven baud rates: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #BAUD, p. 14 ¶ Connector, pins and signal levels: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 7 Mechanical Dimensions and Electrical Interface, drawing and pin table, p. 20 UART levels: 3.0 V, 3.3 V maximum on RXD: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.2 Voltage Tolerance of UART RX Pin (ERRATA), p. 19 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from fdo2::UartInterface<Self> (in inc/fdo2_uart_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the fdo2::UartPort concept, which checks each hook's exact signature and noexcept . A missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the UART up on the first call, 19200 8N1; return true at once afterwards bool Write(const uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) noexcept yes Send all len bytes; false on an error std::size_t Read(uint8_t* data, std::size_t max, uint32_t timeout_ms) noexcept yes Return the bytes received, 0 to max , waiting up to timeout_ms for the first one bool FlushInput() noexcept yes Drop every received byte not yet returned by Read() void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept for the blocking calls Wait at least us microseconds uint32_t NowUs() noexcept no A free-running microsecond counter, wrap-safe; Poll() then takes no argument bool SetBaudRate(uint32_t baud) noexcept no Reconfigure the UART; without it SetBaudRate() returns Unsupported bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept no CtrlPin::Power : ACTIVE powers the module (an external load switch) void Log(LogLevel, const char*) noexcept no Print one line; the message is plain text, never a format string my_port.hpp class MyPort : public fdo2 :: UartInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the UART up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data , len ); } // The number of bytes read (0 to `max`), waiting up to `timeout_ms` for the first one. // The reply length is not known in advance, so this is not an exact-length read. std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t max , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( data , max , timeout_ms ); } // Drop stale bytes before each request. bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_flush_input (); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the module's processing times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules ¶ Raw bytes only. The driver builds the lines and checks the checksum; the port does not parse or retry. Read() returns a count. The reply length is not known in advance, so it is not an exact-length read. It waits for the first byte up to timeout_ms and returns what is in the FIFO. A port whose SDK returns only a status polls the FIFO level first. The receive buffer holds at least 800 bytes ( kRxBufferBytes ): the longest reply. A smaller buffer loses bytes while the driver is busy with something else. FlushInput() really flushes. The driver calls it before each request so a stale byte cannot shift a reply. 19200 baud, 8N1, no flow control at start; the module starts there after every power-up. Without NowUs , call Poll(elapsed_us) ; with it, Poll() ( Non-blocking use ). A hook that returns false is reported as Bus . DelayUs should yield for a millisecond or more on an RTOS (the ESP32 port calls vTaskDelay ), so the other tasks run during the 1.5 s power-up wait. Loopback. A TX line wired to RX echoes every command. The driver does not take an echo of its own #VERS as an answer: the identity must match, so the start-up fails with DeviceIdMismatch or InvalidReply . No power pin. A port whose power pin is not fitted returns true from GpioSet for CtrlPin::Power , a valid no-op (the ESP32 example does so for pin -1). Idle level of the supply switch: INACTIVE (module off) before the output is enabled and before the first line is sent; the port maps ACTIVE to the polarity of your switch. Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the module needs as constexpr values; check your port against them with static_assert , as both example ports do: ports.cpp // The line the port must provide, checked at build time. static_assert ( fdo2 :: kPortDefaultBaud == 19'200U , "8N1 at 19200 baud" ); static_assert ( fdo2 :: kRxBufferBytes >= 800U , "a reply can be 800 characters" ); Constant Value Meaning kPortDefaultBaud 19200 The rate after every power-up kLogicLevelMv 3000 The module's signal level kMaxLogicLevelMv 3300 Absolute maximum on RXD kSupplyMinMv , kSupplyMaxMv 3300, 5000 The supply range kPowerUpMs 1000 The module's power-up time kRxBufferBytes 800 The longest reply A port with every hook ¶ ports.cpp class FullPort : public fdo2 :: UartInterface < FullPort > { public : // Required hooks. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_uart_init (); } bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data , len ); } std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t max , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( data , max , timeout_ms ); } bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_flush_input (); } // Optional hooks: each enables part of the API. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { // the blocking calls and PowerCycle() platform_delay_us ( us ); } uint32_t NowUs () noexcept { // Poll() without an argument return platform_now_us (); } bool SetBaudRate ( uint32_t baud ) noexcept { // SetBaudRate() return platform_uart_set_baud ( baud ); } bool GpioSet ( fdo2 :: CtrlPin pin , fdo2 :: GpioSignal level ) noexcept { // the power pin ( void ) pin ; return platform_gpio_write ( 7 , level == fdo2 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); } void Log ( fdo2 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { ( void ) level ; platform_log ( message ); } }; The ESP-IDF port and the host port are complete examples.

docs.text: Raw bytes only. The driver builds the lines and checks the checksum; the port does not parse or retry. Read() returns a count. The reply length is not known in advance, so it is not an exact-length read. It waits for the first byte up to timeout_ms and returns what is in the FIFO. A port whose SDK returns only a status polls the FIFO level first. The receive buffer holds at least 800 bytes ( kRxBufferBytes ): the longest reply. A smaller buffer loses bytes while the driver is busy with something else. FlushInput() really flushes. The driver calls it before each request so a stale byte cannot shift a reply. 19200 baud, 8N1, no flow control at start; the module starts there after every power-up. Without NowUs , call Poll(elapsed_us) ; with it, Poll() ( Non-blocking use ). A hook that returns false is reported as Bus . DelayUs should yield for a millisecond or more on an RTOS (the ESP32 port calls vTaskDelay ), so the other tasks run during the 1.5 s power-up wait. Loopback. A TX line wired to RX echoes every command. The driver does not take an echo of its own #VERS as an answer: the identity must match, so the start-up fails with DeviceIdMismatch or InvalidReply . No power pin. A port whose power pin is not fitted returns true from GpioSet for CtrlPin::Power , a valid no-op (the ESP32 example does so for pin -1). Idle level of the supply switch: INACTIVE (module off) before the output is enabled and before the first line is sent; the port maps ACTIVE to the polarity of your switch.

Datasheet sections this page relies on UART framing, echo and terminator: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.1 General Definitions, p. 10 Numbers in a reply: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.1 General Definitions, value formats, p. 10 CRC-16/MODBUS suffix: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.2 Detecting communication errors and optional CRC, p. 11 VERS: device, channels, firmware, sensors: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #VERS, p. 11 ¶ IDNR: the unique id: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #IDNR, p. 11 ¶ MOXY: oxygen, temperature, status: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #MOXY, p. 11 ¶ MRAW: phase, signals, pressure, humidity: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #MRAW, p. 12 ¶ LOGO: the status LED: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #LOGO, p. 13 ¶ CRCE: the CRC switch: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #CRCE, p. 14 ¶ Firmware revision history of the G2: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 5 Released Firmware Revisions Changes, p. 18 Firmware revision history: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 5 Released Firmware Revisions Changes, p. 17 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The line ¶ The module starts at 19200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit and no handshake after every power-up. Its signals are 3.0 V; the RXD pin tolerates 3.3 V at most ( Hardware ). Every message is ASCII and ends with one carriage return (CR, 0x0D). The driver ignores a line feed (LF) at the start of a line ( Config::ignore_lf ). A request is a # , a four-letter command and its arguments, separated by single spaces. The module answers with an echo of the command and the values, ended by a CR: #MOXY <CR> request (no argument) #MOXY 211717 21000 1 <CR> reply: oxygen, temperature, status With the checksum on, each reply ends with a colon, a space and a CRC-16 of the line (see Checksum ). Commands ¶ Command What it does Writes flash Repeated after a fault #VERS Device id, channels, firmware, sensors no yes #IDNR The 64-bit unique id (not the serial number) no yes #MOXY Oxygen partial pressure, temperature and the status word no yes #MRAW The same plus phase shift, signal, ambient light, pressure and humidity no yes #LOGO Flashes the module's LED so you can find it no yes #RDUM Reads user memory words no yes #WRUM Writes user memory words yes never #BAUD Changes the baud rate until the next power-up no never #CALO Calibrates the zero point yes never #CAHI Calibrates the high point yes never #CRCE Turns the checksum on or off yes never #BCST Sets the broadcast interval yes never #SETM Sets the measurement mode (FDO2-G2) yes never The driver sends a command that writes flash only when you opted in and the write budget has room ( Calibration ). A repeat of a write after an unclear failure could write twice or hide a half-done change, so the driver never repeats one: it leaves the state as StateUnknown and waits for Resync() . Replies and errors ¶ A failed command answers #ERRO and a code: Code Meaning Driver error Retried -1 General error DeviceError no -21 Command could not be parsed DeviceError yes -22 Receive error DeviceError yes -23 Header error DeviceError yes -26 Command not supported by this firmware Unsupported no any other A code the datasheet calls potentially fatal DeviceFault no -60 Calibration value rejected CalibrationRejected no -26 also teaches the driver: the capability is switched off for the rest of the session ( GetIdentity().caps ). The code itself stays in DeviceErrorCode() . Checksum ¶ With #CRCE 1 the module appends a colon, a space and the checksum to every reply. The checksum is the CRC-16/MODBUS of the characters before the colon. Config::crc says what to expect: Auto learns it from the first #VERS reply, Off never expects it, Required rejects a reply without it. An #ERRO line may come without a checksum ( Config::erro_without_crc ). SetCrcEnabled() turns it on or off ( Settings ). Firmware older than 3.41 forgets the setting at a power cycle ( caps.crc_persistent ). #MOXY 203456 17892 0: 43291 <CR> the checksum covers "#MOXY 203456 17892 0", 43291 in decimal #VERS 8 1 357 15: 17525 <CR> the checksum covers "#VERS 8 1 357 15" Commands carry no checksum; only replies do. The checksum is written in decimal, without leading zeros, after one colon and one space. Grammar the driver enforces ¶ One space between tokens ( Config::strict_spacing ). Numbers are decimal integers; the module sends no decimal point. A line that does not match the command that was asked is dropped and counted as stale ( Counters::stale_lines ). A line with an unknown header parses as Ok with known=false ; the driver counts it as stale and keeps reading, and the fifth one in a request ends it with InvalidReply . A reply that is too long, too short or has the wrong token count is InvalidReply . Next: Status and errors .

Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public fdo2 :: UartInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the UART up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data , len ); } // The number of bytes read (0 to `max`), waiting up to `timeout_ms` for the first one. // The reply length is not known in advance, so this is not an exact-length read. std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t max , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( data , max , timeout_ms ); } // Drop stale bytes before each request. bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_flush_input (); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the module's processing times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method and the optional hooks. 4. Waits for the module's power-up, reads #VERS and #IDNR and checks the device. if ( auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Timeout or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring and the 3 V levels } // 2. One #MOXY: oxygen, temperature and the status word. const auto o = sensor . MeasureOxygen (); if ( ! o ) { return static_cast < int > ( o . error ); // SensorFault: see the status word; OutOfRange; Timeout } o2_mhpa = o . value . o2_mhpa ; // 10^-3 hPa temperature_mc = o . value . temperature_mc ; // 10^-3 degC return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , waits for the module's power-up, reads #VERS and #IDNR and checks that the device is an FDO2 with an oxygen sensor. MeasureOxygen() sends #MOXY and checks the status word and the plausibility windows. The values are integers: oxygen in 0.001 hPa, temperature in 0.001 degC. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. docs.text: Settings ¶ The module's settings that the driver can change: the checksum, the baud rate, the broadcast stream, the measurement mode and the user memory. Datasheet sections this page relies on CRC-16/MODBUS suffix: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.2 Detecting communication errors and optional CRC, p. 11 CRCE: the CRC switch: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #CRCE, p. 14 ¶ RDUM and #WRUM: 64 user words: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #RDUM, #WRUM, p. 14 ¶ BAUD: the eleven baud rates: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #BAUD, p. 14 ¶ BCST: broadcast mode: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #BCST, p. 15 ¶ SETM: measurement modes: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #SETM, p. 15 ¶ Errata: noise at two temperatures: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 6 ERRATA, 6.1 Increased Noise at Specific Temperatures, p. 19 Errata: broadcast send and receive conflict (firmware 3.51): PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.1 Firmware Bug Broadcast Send and Receive Conflict (FW 3.51), p. 19 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Checksum ¶ settings.cpp // Checksummed replies; the driver verifies the change with the next #VERS. fdo2 :: Error TurnOnCrc ( Sensor & sensor ) { return sensor . SetCrcEnabled ( true ). error ; // a flash write: needs consent } SetCrcEnabled() sends #CRCE , a flash write, then a #VERS that must come back as the setting says. With Config::crc set to Auto , the driver follows. See Protocol . Baud rate ¶ settings.cpp // A faster line; the module returns to 19200 baud at every power-up. fdo2 :: Error Faster ( Sensor & sensor ) { const auto r = sensor . SetBaudRate ( 115200 ); // needs the SetBaudRate hook in the port if ( r . error == fdo2 :: Error :: StateUnknown ) { return sensor . Resync (). error ; // tries the new rate, the old one and 19200 } return r . error ; } SetBaudRate() needs the port's SetBaudRate hook; without it the call returns Unsupported . The driver sends #BAUD , switches the port after two character times, and checks with a #VERS . The module returns to 19200 baud at every power-up. If the module does not answer at the new rate, the state is StateUnknown ; Resync() tries the new rate, the old one and 19200. GetConfig().baud follows a successful change. Broadcast ¶ The module can send #MRAW lines by itself at an interval of 100 ms to 10 s ( #BCST ). settings.cpp // The module sends #MRAW lines by itself; read them as they come. fdo2 :: Error Stream ( Sensor & sensor ) { if ( const auto r = sensor . SetBroadcast ( 500 ); ! r ) { // every 500 ms, stored in flash return r . error ; } for ( int i = 0 ; i < 100 ; ++ i ) { platform_delay_us ( 10'000 ); const auto p = sensor . Poll ( 10'000 ); // this port has no clock: pass the elapsed time if ( p . ok () && p . value && sensor . GetRaw (). ok ()) { break ; // one frame decoded } } return sensor . DisableBroadcast (). error ; // waits for a frame boundary first } SetBroadcast(interval_ms) is a flash write and puts the driver in Streaming . In that state every call that sends a command returns Busy until DisableBroadcast() . DisableBroadcast() waits for the end of a frame before it sends #BCST 0 , as the vendor advises, because a command sent in the middle of a frame is lost. A stream left on from an earlier session is found at start-up only if a frame arrives while the driver waits. With broadcast_listen_ms at 0 this covers intervals up to about 250 ms. For a slower stream, set broadcast_listen_ms to at least the interval (up to 12000), or call ProbeBroadcast() . Config::broadcast decides what start-up does when it finds a stream: Refuse returns BroadcastActive , Stream keeps listening, Disable turns it off (a flash write, so it needs consent). Measurement mode ¶ SetMeasurementMode(mode) sends #SETM with a mode of 0 to 4 (a flash write). The FDO2-G2 documents it; the legacy FDO2's datasheet does not, so with Config::family = Family::Fdo2 the driver does not try it. A module that answers #ERRO -26 teaches the driver to stop trying. Modes 0 to 2 answer within 150 ms and every mode within 300 ms ( Config::measurement_ms ). User memory ¶ settings.cpp // 64 words that survive power-off, for your own use. fdo2 :: Error KeepSerial ( Sensor & sensor , int32_t serial ) { const std :: array < int32_t , 1 > word { serial }; if ( const auto r = sensor . WriteUserMemory ( 0 , word ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } std :: array < int32_t , 1 > back {}; return sensor . ReadUserMemory ( 0 , back ). error ; } The module keeps 64 signed 32-bit words that survive power-off. ReadUserMemory() does not write flash. WriteUserMemory() does: it needs consent and counts against the budget ( Calibration ). Power and pending flash writes ¶ A power loss during a flash cycle can corrupt the module's flash (datasheet section 4.3, warning). From the moment the driver sends a flash command until its echo arrives, and for the flash allowance after a lost echo, FlashWritePending() is true. In that time: Deinitialize() returns Busy , because it switches the supply off through the port's power hook. Wait, or call Resync() first. PowerCycle() waits for the flash allowance before it cuts the supply. A failed EnsureInitialized() keeps the supply on. Without the port's power hook the driver cannot cut the supply, and your own switch must follow the same rule. Resynchronise ¶ Resync() recovers a line in an unknown state. It tries each baud rate (the configured one, the one of a lost #BAUD and 19200) with and without the checksum, so a lost #CRCE echo is found whichever setting the module kept. It is allowed while a stream runs (it ends the stream state), and it does not change the identity the driver stored. StreamSilentMs() returns the time since the last stream line, so you can see a stream that has stopped. Identify ¶ Identify() sends #LOGO , which makes the module flash its LED for about a second ( Config::logo_ms ), so you can tell which module on a bench is the one you talk to. Next: Non-blocking use .

docs.text: Status and errors ¶ How the driver turns the module's status word and error replies into values you can act on. Datasheet sections this page relies on Status word bits: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.3 Commands, #MOXY, the status word, p. 12 ERRO codes: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 4.4 Error Codes, Table 1, p. 17 ¶ Errata: error handling of the internal temperature sensor: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.3 Error Handling of Internal Temperature Sensor, p. 20 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The status word ¶ Every #MOXY and #MRAW reply ends with a status word S . The datasheet says S should be 0 or 1. The bits: Bit Level Meaning Status method 0 warning Detector amplification reduced; the reading is valid AmplificationReduced() 1 fatal Oxygen signal too low (below 20 mV) SignalTooLow() 2 fatal Oxygen signal or ambient light too high SignalTooHigh() 3 fatal Reference signal too low (below 20 mV) ReferenceTooLow() 4 fatal Reference signal or ambient light too high (above 2400 mV) ReferenceTooHigh() 5 fatal Temperature sensor failure TemperatureSensorFailed() 7 warning Humidity inside the housing above 90 %RH HumidityHigh() 9 error Pressure sensor failure; the oxygen value is not affected PressureSensorFailed() 10 error Humidity sensor failure; the oxygen value is not affected HumiditySensorFailed() Bits 6, 8 and 11 to 31 are not defined; UndefinedBits() reports them. Status::Classify() gives a Quality : Good (S is 0), Warning (S is 1), Degraded (bit 7, 9 or 10) or Invalid (a fatal or undefined bit). Status policy ¶ Config::status_policy decides which statuses a call accepts: Policy Accepts Everything else Datasheet (default) S of 0 or 1 SensorFault Documented Also bits 7, 9 and 10, as a degraded reading SensorFault Use Documented when you need an oxygen value from a module whose humidity or pressure sensor failed. The bits stay in Oxygen::status either way. status.cpp const char * Describe ( const fdo2 :: Status & status ) { if ( status . SignalTooLow ()) { return "signal too low: the sensor is not covered by the medium or is damaged" ; } if ( status . AmplificationReduced ()) { return "detector amplification reduced: the reading is valid" ; } switch ( status . Classify ()) { case fdo2 :: Quality :: Good : return "good" ; case fdo2 :: Quality :: Degraded : return "a warning bit is set" ; default : break ; } return "do not use the reading" ; } Errors ¶ Every call returns Result<T> with an Error . ToString(error) gives its name. Error When What to do Timeout No complete reply in time Wiring, 3.0 V levels, supply, baud rate Crc The reply's checksum is wrong Noise on the line; the driver already retried a read InvalidReply A line the grammar refuses Check the baud rate and stray bytes SensorFault The status word is not acceptable Read the bits above OutOfRange A value outside the plausibility window Check Config bounds and the medium DeviceError #ERRO -21, -22 or -23 (and -1 on a read) DeviceErrorCode() has the code; -21 to -23 are retried on reads DeviceFault #ERRO with a code the datasheet calls potentially fatal DeviceErrorCode() has the code EchoMismatch The reply echoes other values than were sent Stray bytes or a wrong baud rate DeviceIdMismatch #VERS is not an FDO2 with an oxygen sensor Wrong device or wiring BroadcastActive The module streams and the call needs it silent Config::broadcast policy Unsupported #ERRO -26 , or a missing port hook Older firmware, or a port without the hook CalibrationRejected #ERRO -60 The value is outside the range the module accepts NotPermitted A flash write without consent or past the budget Calibration StateUnknown A flash write or baud change ended with no echo, or an unexpected #ERRO on a flash write Call Resync() NotReady A calibration while the sensor warms up (3 minutes) Wait and call again Busy An operation is pending, or a stream is running Poll until it ends NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded Call it first InvalidArgument An argument or Config field out of range Validate(config) Bus A port hook returned false Your port api_guide.cpp const char * Explain ( fdo2 :: Error error ) { switch ( error ) { case fdo2 :: Error :: Timeout : return "no reply: wiring, 3 V levels, power" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: Crc : return "a corrupted reply: noise on the line" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: SensorFault : return "the status word says the reading is not valid" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: NotPermitted : return "a flash write needs Config::allow_persistent_writes" ; case fdo2 :: Error :: StateUnknown : return "call Resync()" ; default : break ; } return fdo2 :: ToString ( error ); } Counters ¶ GetCounters() returns counters that only grow: transactions, retries, timeouts, CRC errors, invalid replies, device errors, stale lines, broadcast lines, flash writes and bytes discarded. Log them to see a noisy line before it fails. Next: Troubleshooting .

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the module, fuzzers that corrupt what the module sends, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a model of the module in tests/mock_fdo2.hpp : a clock, a receive buffer, the thirteen commands, the status word, the checksum, the broadcast stream and injected faults (silence, corrupted bytes, a late reply, a lost echo, a wrong baud rate, every #ERRO code). They build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DFDO2_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_crc.cpp , test_parse.cpp , test_assembler.cpp , test_encode.cpp The protocol layer alone: CRC-16, grammar, line assembly, command encoding tests/test_status.cpp , test_conversions.cpp , test_capabilities.cpp , test_validate.cpp The status word and policies, unit conversions, firmware capabilities, Config bounds tests/test_lifecycle.cpp , test_faults.cpp , test_errors.cpp Start-up, retries, every error path; every chip-specific Error is returned by some call tests/test_flash.cpp , test_calibration.cpp Consent, the write budget, never repeating a flash write, calibration tests/test_modes.cpp The checksum, the baud rate, resynchronising, the broadcast stream tests/test_safety.cpp An aborted or timed-out start-up never leaves the driver initialised without an identity; docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ What to check when a call fails, by the error it returns. Datasheet sections this page relies on Errata: noise at two temperatures: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2-G2 v5, 6 ERRATA, 6.1 Increased Noise at Specific Temperatures, p. 19 UART levels: 3.0 V, 3.3 V maximum on RXD: PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.2 Voltage Tolerance of UART RX Pin (ERRATA), p. 19 Errata: broadcast send and receive conflict (firmware 3.51): PyroScience Datasheet_FDO2 v21, 6.1 Firmware Bug Broadcast Send and Receive Conflict (FW 3.51), p. 19 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns Bus ¶ A port hook reported a failure. Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the UART pins in your port against the wiring. Check that Write() returns true and sends all the bytes. EnsureInitialized returns Timeout ¶ The module did not answer #VERS . Symptom Likely cause Fix Nothing on TXD No power, or below 3.3 V Check VCC (3.3 V to 5.0 V) and GND Nothing on TXD TX and RX swapped Cross them: MCU TX to RXD, MCU RX to TXD Garbage on TXD The module is at another baud rate Power-cycle it: it starts at 19200 The module streams lines A broadcast is on See below Answers only after a wait A short power_up_ms Raise Config::power_up_ms EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch ¶ #VERS answered, but not as an FDO2 with an oxygen sensor: the device id is not 8 or the sensor bits lack oxygen. Check that the line is not shared with another device. EnsureInitialized returns BroadcastActive ¶ The module streams #MRAW lines ( #BCST is on) and Config::broadcast is Refuse . Set it to Stream to read the frames, or to Disable to turn the stream off (a flash write: it needs allow_persistent_writes ). A slow stream is seen only when broadcast_listen_ms is at least its interval ( Settings ). Calls return Crc now and then ¶ Noise on the line. Shorten the wires, keep them away from the supply and check the ground. The driver already retried a read; GetCounters().crc_errors shows how often it happens. Calls return InvalidReply or EchoMismatch ¶ Bytes that are not part of the reply, or a wrong baud rate. Check that FlushInput() really flushes, that the receive buffer holds 800 bytes and that nothing else writes to the line. Calls return SensorFault ¶ The status word is not acceptable under the status policy. Status and errors lists the bits. With the sensor in air and a signal too low, check that the membrane is clean and uncovered. Calls return StateUnknown ¶ A flash write or a baud change ended with no echo. Call Resync() : it tries the configured rate, the new rate and 19200, each with and without the checksum, and reads #VERS . Then read the setting back before you write it again. Calls return NotPermitted ¶ A flash write needs allow_persistent_writes and room in max_flash_writes ( Calibration ). Calls return Unsupported ¶ The firmware answered #ERRO -26 (it does not know the command), or your port has no hook the call needs ( SetBaudRate ). GetIdentity().caps shows what the firmware offers. Readings look wrong ¶ Within the first three minutes after power-up the accuracy is reduced ( warming_up ). A supply below 3.3 V can make the readings wrong; the module has no supply reading. A calibration at the wrong pressure, humidity or temperature moves every later reading ( Calibration ).

Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. Start-up goes through PoweringUp to Idle. An operation (Start* or a blocking call) puts the driver in Waiting; a good reply returns it to Idle. A timeout, a CRC error or a refused line sends it through Draining, where input is discarded until the line is quiet, so a late reply is never read as the next answer. A flash-writing command or a baud change that ended without a confirmed echo leaves StateUnknown, which only Resync() or a power cycle ends. While the module streams, Idle is reported as Streaming. The driver drops what is in the receive buffer, writes the command and its carriage return, then waits for the module: the module echoes the command, with its values, and ends the reply with one carriage return. The wait is the characters' airtime at the current baud rate, plus the module's processing allowance for the command (command_ms, measurement_ms, calibration_ms, flash_ms or logo_ms of the Config), plus margin_ms. The numbers shown are the Config defaults, read from inc/fdo2_types.hpp. A reply that does not end in time is a Timeout: the driver drains the line, and sends an idempotent read again when retries allow.
